hypothesis: A completed non-camera LLM summary between dialogue requests may increase next dialogue prefill or RAM-cache restoration cost

inputs.W: Fixed authored-public dialogue primer that leaves the same stable prefix as D. Re-prime before every block.
inputs.S: Authored-public ordinary-text summary sent to existing inference lane. Confirm a real model call; do not use structured camera-count fast path.
inputs.D: Exactly the same target dialogue request bytes and options in both arms, inside existing context budget. Never use real history or profiles.

A: Wait matched interval with no summary
D completes; retain numeric response metrics only
B: D completes; retain numeric response metrics only

controls: No overlap of S and D in cache-only experiment. Overlap belongs to a separate queue/preemption experiment.
Same model/build, context, backend settings, request bytes and output bounds; no new model, runner or cache-parameter changes.
W executes before every block, including each consecutive B, to limit carryover effects.
Record quiet interval and any background task. A failed, canceled or still-running S makes this block incomplete.
Do not call a resident-weight warmup request proof that the desired prompt prefix is cached.

Existing host cached-token observation is conditional on output_format; saved normal board dialogue does not explicitly select it. Missing metrics remain unknown. Any supported public-only output_format must be identical in both arms and pass existing request validation.

Paused listening does not stop compaction. Original owner checks existing broker accepted_llm counter before/after each block: expected delta2 for A and3 for B. Extra accepted jobs, failures, cancellations, model restart or incomplete S invalidate the cache-only block. External clients bypassing broker must also be excluded.

Structured local memory completions do not themselves invalidate a cache-only block; record their load changes separately. Broker accepted count is not an exact count of backend jobs that reached GPU execution.
measure: W/S/D request-byte hashes, task kind and numeric completion status
prompt_eval_cached_count when actually returned; missing means unknown
first content / first effective reply-text time from existing stream observation where available
queue wait, S complete-before-D check and RAM-cache restoration metadata if already available; restoration need not be included in prompt_eval_duration
host CPU/GPU pressure and memory-worker model-call count, distinct from completed counter
inference_limits: One active slot is not proof of irreversible KV loss when RAM prompt cache is enabled.
A memory commit is not proof of an LLM request.
Identical public prompt-cache experiment bounds a cache mechanism; it is not a real-dialogue speed guarantee.
Do not attribute other dialogue latency stages or all production overflows to this test.
